 Zerodha co-founder Nikhil Kamath on marriage and kids: ‘I don’t know what I want six months from now’ 
 ETimes.in / Updated: Oct 23, 2026, 15:27 IST Save Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium
 Large
 1 / 4 Marriage, kids or neither? Nikhil Kamath reveals why he isn't planning his future
 Zerodha co-founder Nikhil Kamath isn't rushing down the aisle or setting up a nursery anytime soon. In fact, he's totally fine leaving his future completely unplanned.
 Speaking at the NDTV World Summit 2026, the billionaire entrepreneur got surprisingly candid about why he hesitates to commit to big milestones like marriage or having kids. When asked if his bachelor status is a permanent choice or just a temporary phase, Kamath made it clear that he simply doesn't believe in locking down his entire life years in advance.
 "Nobody knows what they want for life," Kamath said, referencing a conversation with a spiritual speaker earlier at the event. "I don’t know what I want six months from now, let alone five years from now. And I think that’s true for all people."
 by TOI Lifestyle Desk 2 / 4 Why certainty might be a trap
 For Kamath, holding onto rigid beliefs about how life should look is actually a trap. He admitted that he tends to gravitate toward people who aren't afraid to second-guess themselves, ask hard questions, or switch up their minds when new information comes along.
 Too many people, he argued, get emotionally attached to their own opinions and let their egos take over. That kind of stubbornness leaves zero room for personal growth or fresh perspectives. Instead of trying to plot out a rigid master plan for the next decade, he would rather take things as they come and let his opinions evolve naturally.
 3 / 4 Prioritizing freedom over tradition
 Right now, his personal focus is pretty straightforward: he's prioritizing personal freedom and daily peace of mind. He wants enough flexibility on his calendar to chase whatever new interest piques his curiosity, without being tied down by heavy societal obligations or long-term family pressures.
 This isn't the first time Kamath has questioned conventional life paths. He's previously raised eyebrows with his blunt views on traditional parenthood, openly doubting the old-school idea of spending two decades raising kids just to ensure someone looks after you when you get old. On a past podcast, he joked about the financial and emotional gamble of spending 18 years babysitting, only for the kid to turn around at adulthood and walk away anyway.
 4 / 4 Rethinking the idea of legacy
 He's also pretty grounded - if a bit cynical - about the whole concept of leaving a legacy behind. In his eyes, humans tend to vastly overestimate how much they actually matter in the grand scheme of things.
 You arrive, you live your life, you die like every other creature on the planet, and eventually, time moves on without you. So why stress over societal expectations?
 So, will he ever settle down and start a family? Maybe, maybe not. But for now, Nikhil Kamath is completely fine leaving that door unlocked and seeing where life takes him next.
